note: Worked SPARQL queries with the same question in Cypher (shown, not run). at_build is what each returned when the site was built.
prefixes:
PREFIX p: <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/portugal/id/>
PREFIX v: <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/portugal/verb/>
PREFIX t: <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/portugal/type/>
PREFIX a: <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/portugal/prop/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>

queries.title: Nodes by type
queries.note: Every node carries `rdf:type`; the types are the ontology's, with labels in English and Portuguese.
queries.sparql:
SELECT ?type (COUNT(?n) AS ?nodes)
WHERE { ?n a ?type . }
GROUP BY ?type
ORDER BY DESC(?nodes)
queries.cypher:
MATCH (n)
RETURN labels(n)[0] AS type, count(n) AS nodes
ORDER BY nodes DESC

queries.title: Who speaks at the event, listed under which organisation
queries.note: Two edges from the same person. The event is named by its IRI; every node's IRI is its graph id under `portugal/id/`.
queries.cypher:
MATCH (p:Person)-[:SPEAKS_AT]->(:Event {id: 'event:startup-summit-lisbon-2026'}),
      (p)-[:LISTED_UNDER]->(o:Organisation)
RETURN p.label AS person, o.label AS organisation
ORDER BY person

queries.title: A path read aloud in Portuguese
queries.note: The verbs are in the store with `@pt` labels, so the sentence is assembled by the query, not the page. graphs.sgit.ai's rule: if a path does not read as a sentence in the reader's language, the edge is wrong.
queries.sparql:
SELECT ?sessao ?v1 ?evento ?v2 ?local
WHERE {
  ?s a t:Session ; rdfs:label ?sessao ; v:part_of ?e .
  ?e rdfs:label ?evento ; v:takes_place_at ?l .
  ?l rdfs:label ?local .
  v:part_of rdfs:label ?v1 .
  v:takes_place_at rdfs:label ?v2 .
  FILTER(lang(?v1) = "pt" && lang(?v2) = "pt")
}
LIMIT 6
queries.cypher:
MATCH (s:Session)-[r1:PART_OF]->(e:Event)-[r2:TAKES_PLACE_AT]->(l:Place)
RETURN s.label, r1.pt, e.label, r2.pt, l.label
LIMIT 6

queries.title: Walking an edge backwards with a property path
queries.note: `^v:speaks_at` is `hosts` read from the event's side. The store holds each fact once; the inverse is declared with `owl:inverseOf` and walked with `^`.
queries.cypher:
MATCH (e:Event)<-[:SPEAKS_AT]-(p:Person)
RETURN e, count(p) AS speakers

queries.title: The named inverses, from the ontology inside the store
queries.note: The ontology travels with the data. Every verb has a distinct named inverse; a query can prove it rather than a page assert it.
queries.sparql:
SELECT ?verb ?inverse ?verbo
WHERE {
  ?i owl:inverseOf ?v .
  ?v rdfs:label ?verb . FILTER(lang(?verb) = "en")
  ?i rdfs:label ?inverse . FILTER(lang(?inverse) = "en")
  ?v rdfs:label ?verbo . FILTER(lang(?verbo) = "pt")
}
ORDER BY ?verb
queries.cypher:
-- Cypher has no ontology in the store; relationship types are strings.
-- The nearest is CALL db.relationshipTypes(), which returns names without inverses.

queries.title: Everything within two hops of the event
queries.note: A property path over any verb, in either direction, then counted by type. This is the query the SQL console needs a recursive CTE for.
queries.sparql:
SELECT ?type (COUNT(DISTINCT ?n) AS ?nodes)
WHERE {
  <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/portugal/id/event:startup-summit-lisbon-2026> (!(a|rdfs:label)|^!(a|rdfs:label))/(!(a|rdfs:label)|^!(a|rdfs:label)) ?n .
  FILTER(isIRI(?n))
  ?n a ?type .
}
GROUP BY ?type
ORDER BY DESC(?nodes)
queries.cypher:
MATCH (e:Event {id: 'event:startup-summit-lisbon-2026'})-[*1..2]-(n)
RETURN labels(n)[0] AS type, count(DISTINCT n) AS nodes
ORDER BY nodes DESC

queries.title: Sessions grouped by stage
queries.note: `GROUP_CONCAT` over the `on_stage` edge. Sessions the agenda gives no stage do not appear, and that absence is the honest answer.
queries.cypher:
MATCH (s:Session)-[:ON_STAGE]->(st:Stage)
RETURN st.label AS stage, collect(s.label) AS sessions

queries.title: The press pages and who publishes them
queries.note: Coverage nodes carry the publisher as a property and `covers` the event as an edge; the Organisation behind each is reached through `published_by`.
queries.cypher:
MATCH (c:Coverage)-[:COVERS]->(:Event {id: 'event:startup-summit-lisbon-2026'}),
      (c)-[:PUBLISHED_BY]->(o:Organisation)
RETURN o.label AS publisher, c.label AS title, c.published
ORDER BY c.published, publisher

queries.title: Who is no longer listed
queries.note: The boolean is typed `xsd:boolean` in the triples, so `true` matches as a literal. There is no reason property to ask for.
queries.cypher:
MATCH (p:Person {no_longer_listed: true})
RETURN p.label AS person, p.source AS source

queries.title: CONSTRUCT the inverse edges on the fly
queries.note: The store holds 298 forward edges. This query builds the 298 inverse ones as new triples without storing them; the console shows what came back.
queries.cypher: -- No Cypher equivalent: inverses are not declared, so nothing can construct them.

queries.title: ASK: is any edge symmetric?
queries.note: graphs.sgit.ai bans symmetric edges (`related_to`, `associated_with`). The answer should be false; the rule is a query, not a promise.
queries.cypher:
MATCH (x)-[r]->(y)-[s]->(x)
WHERE type(r) = type(s)
RETURN count(*) > 0 AS symmetric
